semantically_equivalent_models.justification: The "dynamic deformable attention network" is a model that incorporates concepts of dynamic changes in attention, aligning with compositional attention which focuses on rearranging and constructing attention weights. Both models deal with dynamic and flexible attention patterns.

While multi-head attention is a broader mechanism used in models, compositional attention involves creating new attention patterns by combining different attentions. Multi-head can be viewed as a component or equivalent approach to compositional attention due to its capability to capture information from various representation subspaces.

parent_models.justification: Compositional attention falls under a broader category of attention-based models as it fundamentally relies on computing attention scores to prioritize information.

This model incorporates attentive mechanisms, similar to compositional attention, but with emphasis on constant memory which can be a parent of varied attention schemas including compositional attention.

closest_parent_model.justification: Compositional attention is fundamentally concerned with manipulating and utilizing attention scores which clearly anchors it within the broader category of "attention-based models." This makes "attention-based models" the semantically closest parent.

child_models.justification: This model integrates attention mechanisms with LSTM, focusing on adjusting the neural network pathways via attention. It is more specific than general compositional attention.

closest_sibling_model.justification: "Recurrent attention model" is strongly aligned due to its focus on managing dynamic attention sequences over time, sharing a fundamental approach with compositional and rearranging attention strategies.
